# PG101 — BaseModel uses no Pydantic surface (advisory, opt-in)

Activation: opt-in via `--extend-select=PG101` (off in the default select set).

## Cause

A `BaseModel` subclass uses none of the features that justify a `BaseModel`
rather than a stdlib `@dataclass`: no `model_config`, no `Field(...)`, no
`Annotated` field, no validator/serializer/`computed_field` decorator, no
`__pydantic_extra__`, no `model_*` override. Per the guidance model, internal
code-built data that crosses no untrusted boundary is better as a stdlib
`@dataclass`. `RootModel` subclasses are excluded.

## Fix

If the data is internal, code-built state, use a stdlib `@dataclass`. If it sits
at an untrusted boundary (external/JSON/LLM input, caller args), add the
Pydantic surface that earns the `BaseModel` (validators, config, fields) — which
also silences this hint.

```python
# Flagged — internal state, no Pydantic surface
class State(BaseModel):
    user_id: int
    name: str


# Option A — internal: stdlib dataclass
@dataclass
class State:
    user_id: int
    name: str


# Option B — boundary: add surface (e.g. frozen config)
class State(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
    user_id: int
    name: str
```

## Suppression

This hint is opt-in; to silence one occurrence while it is selected, use
`# noqa: PG101` on the class line.
